items.title: AP sources: Staff at U.S. center for AI safety are reporting to the White House, raising independence concerns
items.excerpt: Two former officials told AP that staff at the Commerce Department's AI standards center (CAISI) were asked to informally report to a White House office. The center has no permanent leader and has stopped publishing research. The White House pointed to Trump's Super Intelligence Force and a PCAST report it commissioned.
items.rationale: Policy axis: AP reports that the U.S. federal AI evaluation body (CAISI) has lost its independence, citing named-role sources. That affects how the U.S. government tests frontier models. The claims are attributed to the former officials and to the White House.

items.title: Russia and US seek to block plan for binding rules on autonomous weapons
items.excerpt: Russia and the US are seeking to block a plan for a legally binding instrument on lethal autonomous weapons ahead of a UN conference this month, seen as a key moment after years of talks on filling the governance gap for AI weapons systems.
items.rationale: Geopolitics axis: the US and Russia are positioning to block a binding treaty on AI weapons ahead of this month's UN conference. This is a separate event from the 10-22 UN military-AI initiative card.

items.title: Foster bill would bolster tech use to monitor AI financial risks
items.excerpt: Rep. Bill Foster (D-Ill.) introduced legislation Thursday to help financial regulators use technology to spot financial stress turbocharged by AI and around-the-clock payment systems.
items.rationale: Policy axis: a new federal bill (a concrete filing) on how financial regulators should monitor AI-driven market stress. It sits next to the 11-06 OCC framework but is a separate legislative action.

items.title: Singapore authorities urge strict limits on AI agent autonomy, access to personal accounts
items.excerpt: An advisory issued Nov 6 by Singapore's Cyber Security Agency, GovTech and IMDA tells consumers to connect only necessary apps to personal AI agents, restrict sensitive accounts and require permission before deleting or sharing files; it follows the Singapore launch of Meta Muse.
items.rationale: Policy axis: an official multi-agency government advisory that sets permission limits for personal AI agents. It gives builders of agent products concrete guidance, and it is unrelated to the 10-30 Pentagon agent incident.

items.title: State to scrap ticketless AI parking fines following errors
items.excerpt: The South Australian government will overhaul council use of AI-assisted camera cars, scrapping ticketless parking fines that arrive by mail weeks later after a high rate of challenged fines were withdrawn.
items.rationale: Policy axis: a state government decision to roll back automated AI enforcement after error rates came to light. It is a concrete public-sector AI accountability action.
